ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r1.claim: Affluent leaders of Makkah and Ṭāʾif mistook wealth for proof that they were God's favorites and expected still more; Muhammad should leave their fate to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r1.anchor: These verses admonish the megalomaniac leaders of Makkah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r4.claim: The passage describes a general wealthy, high-status mentality, not Walīd ibn Mughīrah alone, though it applies to him too.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p41/r4.anchor: there is no reason for restricting the verse to him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r4.claim: God also gave him sons who supported his many business ventures; in tribal society family numbers and defense were central to status and survival.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r4.anchor: supporters in every place and front

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r5.claim: The description of the sons as present points to their being capable and alert enough to stand by their father when needed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p42/r5.anchor: the sons too had to be so capable and alert that they could stand by the side of their father whenever any need arose

RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r1.claim: One reading is that his sons stayed constantly with him in Mecca: as wealthy men they need not leave to earn a living, and their presence comforted him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r1.anchor: بنين حضورا معه بمكة لا يفارقونه البتة لأنهم كانوا أغنياء فما كانوا محتاجين إلى مفارقته لطلب كسب ومعيشة

RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, “witnessing” means the sons were men who accompanied him to public gatherings and assemblies.
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r2.anchor: أنهم رجال يشهدون معه المجامع والمحافل

RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r3.claim: Mujāhid says al-Walīd had ten sons.
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r3.anchor: وعن مجاهد : كانوا عشرة ، وقيل : سبعة

RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r4.claim: Another report counts seven sons and names them as al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd, Khālid, ʿUmāra, Hishām, al-ʿĀṣ, Qays, and ʿAbd Shams.
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r4.anchor: وقيل : سبعة كلهم رجال الوليد بن الوليد وخالد وعمارة وهشام والعاص وقيس وعبد شمس

RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r5.claim: Of the seven named sons, Khālid, ʿUmāra, and Hishām became Muslims.
RAZI-FULL:v30p175#3/r5.anchor: أسلم منهم ثلاثة خالد وعمارة وهشام

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r6.claim: The verses are applied specifically to al-Walīd’s great wealth, seven or ten sons, learning, and eloquence among Quraysh.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r6.anchor: These verses are said to refer specifically to the great fortune that God had bestowed upon al-Walīd, who was among the wealthiest men in Makkah

TAB-FULL:v23p424/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p424/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p424/r1.claim: Mujāhid says al-Walīd had ten sons who were present with him.
TAB-FULL:v23p424/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وبنين شهودا} [المدثر: 13] قال: كان بنوه عشرة

TABATABAI:74:12-25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r2.claim: Shuhūdan means present: he sees his sons and draws strength from them; the phrase is coordinated with wealth.
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r2.anchor: أي حضورا يشاهدهم ويتأيد بهم، وهو عطف على قوله { مالا }

BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r7.claim: Shuhūd is the plural of shāhid, meaning present; al-Walīd’s sons were with him in Mecca.
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r7.anchor: جمع شاهد مثل قاعد وقعود وشهده

BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r8.claim: Their presence means either that they stayed with him for his enjoyment and were spared work by his wealth, or that they attended gatherings and enhanced his standing.
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r8.anchor: أو حضورا معه في الأندية والمحافل لوجاهتهم واعتبارهم

BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r9.speaker: المفسرون
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r9.claim: Exegetes say al-Walīd had ten sons, three of whom converted: Khālid, Hishām, and ʿAmāra.
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r9.anchor: وكان له عشرة بنين أسلم منهم ثلاثة خالد وهشام وعمارة قاله المفسرون

BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r10.speaker: المحدثون
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r10.claim: Hadith scholars say al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd converted, while ʿAmāra died an unbeliever at Badr or in Abyssinia at the Negus’s hand.
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r10.anchor: وأطبق المحدثون على أن الوليد بن الوليد أسلم

BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r11.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r11.claim: Al-Suhaylī names Hishām ibn al-Walīd, al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd, and Khālid ibn al-Walīd among the three; he leaves unnamed those who died in paganism.
BURSEVI:v10p175#2/r11.anchor: قال السهيلي رحمه الله هم هشام بن الوليد والوليد بن الوليد

BURSEVI:v10p176/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p176/r1.claim: The Najmī allusion makes al-Walīd the solitary evil soul; his wealth, bad traits, followers, and prestige symbolize sins and the dark natural powers of a rebellious self.
BURSEVI:v10p176/r1.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : يشير إلى الوليد بن مغيرة

BURSEVI:v10p176/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p176/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p176/r2.claim: Abū Bakr the hidden, ʿUmar the spirit, ʿUthmān the secret, and ʿAlī the heart use spiritual light to erase the self’s darkness, defeat its deeds and followers, and end its dominion.
BURSEVI:v10p176/r2.anchor: يعني دعني وإياه فإني أسلط عليه أبا بكر الخفي وعمر الروح وعثمان السر وعلى القلب

TABRISI:74:11-31/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:11-31/r12.claim: His sons were present with him in Mecca and did not travel for commerce because their wealth made it unnecessary.
TABRISI:74:11-31/r12.anchor: حضورا معه بمكة لا يغيبون عنه لغناهم عن ركوب السفر للتجارة

TABRISI:74:11-31/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:74:11-31/r13.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says al-Walid had thirteen sons.
TABRISI:74:11-31/r13.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: كانوا ثلاثة عشر

TABRISI:74:11-31/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31/r14.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:74:11-31/r14.claim: Muqatil says al-Walid had seven sons and names them; Khalid, Hisham, and ʿUmārah became Muslim.
TABRISI:74:11-31/r14.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كانوا سبعة الوليد وخالد وعمارة وهشام والعاص وقيس وعبد شمس

TABRISI:74:11-31/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31/r15.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:74:11-31/r15.claim: The report says al-Walid’s wealth and children continued to decline after this passage until his death.
TABRISI:74:11-31/r15.anchor: قالوا فما زال الوليد بعد هذه الآية في نقصان من ماله وولده حتى هلك

THALABI:v10p71/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p71/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p71/r10.claim: The sons were with al-Walid in Mecca and did not leave his side.
THALABI:v10p71/r10.anchor: بنين شهودا حضورا معه بمكة لا يغيبون عنه

THALABI:v10p71/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p71/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v10p71/r11.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr counts thirteen sons.
THALABI:v10p71/r11.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: كانوا ثلاثة عشر ولدا. مجاهد وقتادة: كانوا عشرة.

THALABI:v10p71/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p71/r12.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
THALABI:v10p71/r12.claim: Mujahid and Qatada count ten sons.
THALABI:v10p71/r12.anchor: مجاهد وقتادة: كانوا عشرة. مقاتل: كانوا سبعة كلهم رجال، وهم:

THALABI:v10p71/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p71/r13.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v10p71/r13.claim: Mujahid counts seven sons, all male, names them, and says Khalid, Hisham, and ʿUmara embraced Islam.
THALABI:v10p71/r13.anchor: مقاتل: كانوا سبعة كلهم رجال، وهم: الوليد بن الوليد وخالد بن الوليد وعماره بن الوليد

THALABI:v10p71/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p71/r14.speaker: قالوا
THALABI:v10p71/r14.claim: They say that after this verse was revealed, al-Walid kept losing wealth and children until his death.
THALABI:v10p71/r14.anchor: قالوا: فما زال الوليد بعد نزول هذه الآية في نقصان من ماله وولده حتى هلك.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-Walid had ten sons present in Mecca who did not travel; al-Kalbi, Mujahid, and Qatada agree.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان له عشرة أولاد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r8.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says al-Walid had thirteen sons.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r8.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: كانوا ثلاثة عشر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r9.claim: Muqatil says al-Walid had seven sons.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r10.claim: Abu Ishaq says the sons were with their father and did not need to go away.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p420/r10.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: أي شهود معه لا يحتاجون أن يتصرفوا ويغيبوا عنه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r3.claim: He had ten sons present with him in Mecca.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r3.anchor: { وبنين شهودا } حضورا معه بمكة، وكانوا عشرة.

ELMALILI:74:13/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:13/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:13/r1.claim: Shuhud is the plural of shahid: sons present with their father, free to attend gatherings and consulted for testimony, opinions, and knowledge.
ELMALILI:74:13/r1.anchor: hazır hepsi yanında, göz önünde, çalışmak için

ELMALILI:74:13/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:13/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:13/r2.claim: Reports say al-Walid had ten or thirteen adult sons; seven are identified: Walid, Khalid, Umara, Hisham, As, Qays, and Abd Shams.
ELMALILI:74:13/r2.anchor: Denilmiş ki Velîd b. Mugīre’nin hepsi ricâlden olmak üzere on veya on üç oğlu vardı, fakat mâlum olan yedidir

ELMALILI:74:13/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:13/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:13/r3.claim: One report says Khalid, Hisham, and Walid embraced Islam.
ELMALILI:74:13/r3.anchor: Denilmiş ki: Bunlardan Hâlid, Hişam, Velîd[^2] şeref-i İslâm ile müşerref olmuşlar

ELMALILI:74:13/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:13/r4.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
ELMALILI:74:13/r4.claim: Al-Kashshaf instead names Khalid, Hisham, and Umara as the three sons who embraced Islam.

ELMALILI:74:13/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:13/r5.speaker: آلوسي
ELMALILI:74:13/r5.claim: Alusi reports disagreement over whether Umara was killed at Badr or in Abyssinia by the Negus, but says both accounts agree he died an unbeliever.
ELMALILI:74:13/r5.anchor: Âlûsî der ki: “Umâre’nin Bedir’de veya Habeşte Necâşî tarafından katledildiği ihtilâflıdır, iki rivayet de kâfiren katlinde müttefiktir

ELMALILI:74:13/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:13/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:13/r6.claim: Alusi rejects al-Thalabi's report from Muqatil that Umara converted; Ibn Hajar calls it an error, also repeated in al-Kashshaf and by its followers.
ELMALILI:74:13/r6.anchor: İslâmına dair Sa‘lebî’nin Mukātil’den rivayeti sahih olmaz, İbn Hacer onun galat olduğunu tansis etmiştir. Bu galat sâhib-i Keşşâf’ta da vâki‘olmuş

ELMALILI:74:13/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:13/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:13/r7.claim: Alusi notes with surprise that Walid ibn Walid was omitted despite hadith scholars unanimously affirming his conversion.
ELMALILI:74:13/r7.anchor: Taaccüb olunur ki Velîd b. Velîd’i İslâm ile müşerref olanlar meyânında zikretmemişler, hâlbuki muhaddisîn baştan âhire onun islâmında müttefiktirler

ELMALILI:74:13/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:13/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:13/r8.claim: Elmalılı concludes that Walid ibn Walid later converted, Umara's conversion is disputed, and the remaining sons beyond four are unknown.
ELMALILI:74:13/r8.anchor: Velîd b. Velîd’in de sonradan islâmında ihtilâf görülmüyor fakat Umâre ihtilâflı, dörtten mâ‘adâsı ise gayr-i mâlum

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r2.claim: Al-Walīd was a wealthy Quraysh notable with many sons, yet instead of thanking God for His gifts he was ungrateful to God and the Prophet and led efforts to suppress Islam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r2.anchor: Velîd, Kureyş’in ileri gelenlerinden olup çok sayıda oğulları vardı ve oldukça zengindi; buna rağmen Allah’ın kendisine lutfettiği nimetlere şükredecek yerde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.claim: The passage’s general lesson is that gratitude to the giver of blessings is a basic moral duty grounded in reason and justice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r5.anchor: Nimete karşı şükretmek, nimet sahibine minnettar olmak en yalın ahlâkî ödevlerden biri, akıl ve adalet gereğidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.claim: Failing to thank God for life and material and spiritual gifts is grave ingratitude, especially when it advances denial, polytheism, and injustice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:11/r6.anchor: varlığımızı, hayatımızı, sahip olduğumuz, yararlandığımız her türlü maddî ve mânevî nimet ve imkânları lutfeden Allah’a minnettar olmamak, şükretmemek

QUSHAYRI:v3p363/r21.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p363/r21.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p363/r21.claim: His sons are present with him and need not travel away.
QUSHAYRI:v3p363/r21.anchor: حضورا معه لا يحتاجون إلى السفر

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#3/r3.claim: The passage refers to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who had ten sons present with him and not away on trade or work.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p496#3/r3.anchor: وهو الوليد بن المغيرة: كان له عشرة بنين (2) لا يغيبون عنه في تجارة ولا عمل

NAHHAS:v5p65/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p65/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p65/r19.claim: After movement, the alif of connection is dropped; lineage forms include بنوي, while Sibawayh permits ابني and some Kufans forbid it.
NAHHAS:v5p65/r19.anchor: لما تحركت حذفت ألف الوصل وعلى هذا قالوا في النسب بنوي

ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r9.claim: His sons were present with him, so they did not need to travel away on errands.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r9.anchor: وبنين شهودا، أي شهود معه لا يحتاجون إلى أن يتصرفوا

ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r10.claim: The passage is said to refer to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who had ten sons and was wealthy.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246/r10.anchor: وهذا قيل يعنى به الوليد بن المغيرة، كان له بنون عشرة وكان موسرا

ASAD-NOTES:74:11/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:11/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:11/r3.claim: God gave him children who are present as witnesses of his affection.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.claim: Meccan opponents repeatedly alleged that the Quran was human fabrication, borrowed ancient lore, or material copied from earlier writings and dictated to Muhammad; the Quran records these charges and reasons against their falsehood.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p62/r1.anchor: ويسجل القرآن مفترياتهم لا يكتمها، ويجادلهم فيها بما يهدي كل ذي عقل وبصيرة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.claim: Al-Muddaththir is the counterpart of the preceding al-Muzzammil; their central themes are essentially the same and their names share a meaning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r1.anchor: There is no essential difference between the central themes of both sūrahs .

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.claim: Verses 11–17 warn that Judgment Day will be severe for disbelievers who presume their wealth and rank will bring them still more.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r6.anchor: The Prophet (sws) should well inform the people about the afflictions of the Day of Judgement.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r8.claim: God later bestowed wealth and status, but instead of gratitude the man became conceited and vain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p31/r8.anchor: conceit and vanity overcame them and they held that whatever they had was their right by birth

IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.claim: At the pilgrimage season, Quraysh ask al-Walid for a single story about Muhammad; after rejecting soothsayer, madman, poet, and sorcerer as accurate descriptions, he recommends calling him a sorcerer because people see him as dividing families.
IBNHISHAM:v1p270/r1.anchor: ثم إن الوليد بن المغيرة اجتمع إليه نفر من قريش، وكان ذا سن فيهم، وقد حضر الموسم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r13.claim: The sons may be “present” because they stayed in Mecca with their wealthy father, whose company comforted him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r13.anchor: أي حضورا معه بمكة لا يظعنون عنه لغناهم فهو مستأنس بهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r14.claim: Alternatively, they attended gatherings and public assemblies with their father.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r14.anchor: أو شهودا: أي رجالا يشهدون معه المجامع والمحافل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r15.claim: A third interpretation makes them witnesses whose testimony was heard in disputes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r15.anchor: أو تسمع شهادتهم فيما يتحاكم فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r16.claim: Reports vary on their number and name Khalid, Hishām, ʿUmāra, al-Walīd, al-ʿĀṣ, Qays, and ʿAbd Shams; the first three accepted Islam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r16.anchor: واختلف في عددهم، فذكر منهم: خالد وهشام وعمارة، وقد أسلموا والوليد والعاصي وقيس وعبد شمس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r17.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r17.claim: Muqātil says al-Walīd’s wealth and children declined after revelation until his death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p328/r17.anchor: قال مقاتل: فما زال الوليد بعد هذه الآية وبعد نزولها في نقص في ماله وولده حتى هلك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r1.claim: His sons were present with him in Mecca and did not leave to manage work or trade, since his abundant wealth and servants made that unnecessary.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r1.anchor: حضورا معه بمكة يتمتع بمشاهدتهم لا يفارقونه للتصرف في عمل أو تجارة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r2.claim: “Present” may instead mean that the sons attended public gatherings with him, lending him standing and influence.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that the sons could testify in legal disputes.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r3.anchor: أو تسع شهاداتهم فيما يتحاكم فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid says al-Walīd had ten sons; other reports give thirteen or seven.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r4.anchor: واختلف في عددهم فعن مجاهد أنهم عشرة وقيل ثلاثة عشر وقيل سبعة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r5.claim: In the seven-son report, al-Walīd b. al-Walīd, Khālid, and Hishām converted to Islam; the reports differ over how al-Walīd died but agree that he died an unbeliever.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r5.anchor: وقد أسلم هؤلاء الثلاثة والعاص وقيس وعبد شمس وعمارة واختلفت الرواية فيه أنه قتل يوم بدر أو قتله النجاشي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r6.speaker: الثعلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r6.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī’s report from Muqātil that al-Walīd converted is unsound; Ibn Ḥajar calls it an error, repeated by al-Kashshāf and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r6.anchor: ورواية الثعلبي عن مقاتل إسلامه لا تصح ونص ابن حجر على أن ذلك غلط وقد وقع في هذا الغلط صاحب الكشاف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī also faults those accounts for omitting al-Walīd b. al-Walīd from the converts, although hadith scholars unanimously say he converted.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p122#2/r7.anchor: والعجب أيضا أنهم لم يذكروا الوليد بن الوليد فيمن أسلم مع أن المحدثين عن آخرهم أطبقوا على إسلامه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r1.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r1.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say his ten sons lived near him in Mecca and were always present.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r2.claim: Muqatil says there were seven sons and names them; three—Khalid, Hisham, and ʿUmara—became Muslims.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p267/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كانوا سبعة وهم الوليد بن الوليد وخالد وعمارة وهشام والعاص وقيس وعبد شمس، أسلم منهم [ثلاثة] (1) خالد وهشام و [عمارة] (2)

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r7.claim: His sons were present with him in Mecca, so he enjoyed their company and they needed neither to travel for work nor be sent on errands.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r7.anchor: حضورا معه بمكة يتمتع بلقائهم لا يحتاجون إلى سفر لطلب المعاش

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r8.claim: Alternatively, the sons were present at gatherings and assemblies, where their standing and respect mattered.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r8.anchor: أو في المحافل والأندية لوجاهتهم واعتبارهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r9.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r9.claim: It is said al-Walīd had ten or more adult sons; three—Khālid, ʿUmāra, and Hishām—became Muslims.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:11-13/r9.anchor: قيل كان له عشرة بنين أو أكثر كلهم رجال، فأسلم منهم ثلاثة خالد وعمارة وهشام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r8.claim: After abundant wealth, sons—especially male children—are a foremost worldly desire; their presence spared him travel and let him enjoy their company whenever he wished.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r8.anchor: أول ما يمتد إليه النفس بعد كثرة المال الولد , وكان أحب الولد الذكر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r9.claim: Shuhud means the sons were constantly present, intelligent and capable, and prominent in gatherings, as though no one else attended.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r9.anchor: أي حضورا معه لغناه عن الأسفار بكثرة المال وانتشار الخدم وقوة الأعوان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r10.claim: One of al-Walid’s sons, Khalid, later embraced Islam and became the sword of God and His Messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p224/r10.anchor: منهم خالد الذي من الله بإسلامه , فكان سيف الله تعالى وسيف رسوله

DURR-FULL:v8p329/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r4.claim: Mujahid says al-Walid had ten sons who were present and did not stay away.
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

DURR-FULL:v8p329/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r10.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r10.claim: Abu Malik says al-Walid had thirteen sons.
DURR-FULL:v8p329/r10.anchor: عن أبي مالك {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} قال: الوليد بن المغيرة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r4.claim: Mujahid says al-Walīd had ten sons, who were present with him and never absent.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r4.anchor: وبنين قال : كانوا عشرة شهودا قال : لا يغيبون

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r9.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr identifies the man as al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra b. Hishām al-Makhzūmī and says he had thirteen sons, each a household head.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3382#4/r9.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا الايات ، قال : هو الوليد بن المغيرة بن هشام المخزومي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p304/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p304/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p304/r5.claim: His sons were ‘present’ because they stayed with him, comforted him, attended gatherings as a source of pride, and needed no livelihood from travel, trade, or raiding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p304/r5.anchor: ووصفهم بشهود جمع شاهد ، أي حاضر ، أي لا يفارقونه فهو مستأنس بهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p304/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p304/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p304/r6.claim: Reports differ on the number of al-Walid's sons: one says ten and another thirteen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p304/r6.anchor: قيل : كان له عشرة بنين وقيل ثلاثة عشر ابنا ، والمذكور منهم سبعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p304/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p304/r7.speaker: ابن حزم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p304/r7.claim: Ibn Hazm's Genealogy lists six sons, omitting al-Asi from the seven named here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p304/r7.anchor: ولم يذكر ابن حزم في ( جمهرة الأنساب ) : العاصي . واقتصر على ستة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r10.claim: شهودا means sons who are present and continually at hand.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r11.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r11.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say al-Walid had ten children.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r11.anchor: قال مجاهد وقتادة: كان له عشرة من الولد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r12.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p394/r12.claim: Ibn Jubayr says al-Walid had thirteen children.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405/r1.claim: The sons were present with him, so he did not need them to travel for work and be away from him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى وبنين شهودا أي حضروا معه لا يحتاجون إلى التصرف والسفر فيغيبوا عنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405/r2.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405/r2.anchor: وفي عددهم أربعة أقوال أحدها عشرة قاله مجاهد وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405/r3.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p405/r3.anchor: والثاني ثلاثة عشر قاله ابن جبير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r7.claim: Mujahid explains “present sons” as sons who do not go away; they remain with their father rather than travel for trade, while their servants and hired workers do the trading.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r7.anchor: قال مجاهد: لا يغيبون، أي: حضورا عنده لا يسافرون في التجارات، بل مواليهم وأجراؤهم يتولون ذلك عنهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r8.claim: Their remaining seated with their father allowed him to enjoy and take delight in them, making their presence an added blessing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r8.anchor: وهم قعود عند أبيهم، يتمتع بهم ويتملى بهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r9.speaker: السدي وأبو مالك وعاصم بن عمر بن قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r9.claim: Al-Suddi, Abu Malik, and ʿAsim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatada report that the man had thirteen sons.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r9.anchor: وكانوا -فيما ذكره السدي، وأبو مالك، وعاصم بن عمر بن قتادة-ثلاثة عشر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid report that the man had ten sons.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p265#2/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، ومجاهد: كانوا عشرة. وهذا أبلغ في النعمة

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.claim: The passage is said to concern al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, wealthy with sons and called al-Wahid among his people, according to Ibn Amir.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.anchor: قيل: نزلت هذه الآيات في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، وكان له مال وبنون، قال ابن عامر: وكان يسمى الوحيد في قومه،

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.claim: In the story, al-Walid rejects calling Muhammad a soothsayer, poet, or madman, then chooses “magician” and says the Qur’an separates families.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.anchor: ثم اختلفوا، فقيل: إنه أتى قريشا في ناديها، وقال: هذا الموسم، والناس يسألون عن محمد،

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r1.claim: Abundant blessings make disobedience toward the Benefactor more serious.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r1.anchor: تدل الآيات على أن كثرة النعم توجب عظم عصيان المنعم.

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r2.claim: God grants blessings to unbelievers, contrary to the Mujbira.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن لله تعالى على الكفار نعما، خلاف قول المجبرة.

JISHUMI:v10p7160/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r3.claim: Worldly conditions and goods are blessings from God.
JISHUMI:v10p7160/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن أحوال الدنيا من نعمه تعالى.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r13.claim: His sons were present in Mecca instead of traveling for work; wealth spared them earning and spared him worry and separation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r13.anchor: حضورا معه بمكة لا يفارقونه للتصرف في عمل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r14.claim: Alternatively, they were men who attended public gatherings or whose testimony was heard in disputes.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r15.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r15.claim: Mujāhid says al-Walīd had ten sons.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r15.anchor: وعن مجاهد : كان له عشرة بنين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r16.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r16.claim: Other reports give thirteen sons or seven, naming them; three of the seven, Khālid, Hishām, and ʿUmāra, became Muslims.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p649/r16.anchor: وقيل : ثلاثة عشر . وقيل : سبعة كلهم رجال

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r16.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r16.claim: Al-Suddi says al-Walid had ten sons.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r16.anchor: أحدها : أنهم كانوا عشرة , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r17.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r17.claim: Al-Dahhak says he had seven children born in Mecca and five in Taif.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r17.anchor: الثاني : قال الضحاك : كان له سبعة ولدوا بمكة , وخمسة ولدوا بالطائف .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r18.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r18.claim: Ibn Jubayr says he had thirteen sons.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r18.anchor: الثالث : أنهم كانوا ثلاثة عشر رجلا , قاله ابن جبير .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r19.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r19.claim: Al-Suddi says the sons were present with their father and did not leave him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r19.anchor: أحدها : أنهم حضور معه لا يغيبون عنه , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r20.claim: Ibn Abbas says when al-Walid was mentioned, his sons were mentioned with him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r20.anchor: الثاني : أنه إذا ذكر ذكروا معه , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r21.speaker: ابن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r21.claim: Ibn Jubayr says each son was a household head.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r21.anchor: الثالث : أنهم كلهم رب بيت , قاله ابن جبير .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r22.claim: Another possibility is that the sons had become like him in witnessing and carrying out his affairs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p139/r22.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : أنهم قد صاروا مثله من شهود ما كان يشهده , والقيام بما كان يباشره

MUQATIL:74:11-17/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:11-17/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:11-17/r3.claim: His sons were present and never away from him, since their wealth and business were in Mecca; Muqatil names seven sons, including Khalid, who later converted.
MUQATIL:74:11-17/r3.anchor: يعني حضورا لا يغيبون أبدا عنه في تجارة ولا غيرها لكثرة أموالهم بمكة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#2/r1.claim: His ten sons were present with him in Mecca because they were wealthy enough not to travel for work; Khalid, Hisham, and Amara became Muslims.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#2/r1.anchor: حضورا معه بمكة لغناهم عن السفر وكانوا عشرة أسلم منهم خالد وهشام وعمارة

QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r17.claim: The sons are present with al-Walid and do not leave while he conducts his affairs.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r17.anchor: أي حضورا لا يغيبون عنه في تصرف

QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r18.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r18.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say ten sons; al-Suddi and al-Dahhak say twelve, including seven born in Mecca and five in Taif; Saʿid says thirteen.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r19.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r19.claim: Muqatil says seven sons, all male, and three converted: Khalid, Hisham, and al-Walid ibn al-Walid; their father’s wealth and children declined until he died.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:11-13/r19.anchor: مقاتل: كانوا سبعة كلهم رجال، أسلم منهم ثلاثة: خالد وهشام
